newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks post record as cyclicals shine.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks post record as cyclicals shine.

text.p: Swiss shares came off intra-day peaks but still closed at record highs on Monday, powered by strong cyclical shares that made up for negelected banks, dealers said.
The broad Swiss Performance Index ended up 22.70 points at a record close at 2,549.31 after touching an intra-day all-time high of 2,550.89.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index advanced 28.1 points to a record close at 3,975.5 after hitting an all-time high at 3,983.5 during the day.
The firm dollar and higher prices on Wall Street supported sentiment, dealers said, but the market was still cautious ahead of Tuesday's U.S. consumer price figures for December.

Banks were under some pressure from technical factors and because of the ongoing row over dormant Jewish wealth and looted Nazi gold that has sparked Jewish groups to threaten a boycott of Swiss financial institutions, dealers said.
Technical factors included the expiry of options and futures on Soffex an Friday, which coincides with several expiring warrants on UBS shares.
Union Bank of Switzerland lost 16 Swiss francs to 1,154. Credit Suisse Group rose 0.25 francs to 134.75. Swiss Bank Corp shed 2.75 to 248.25.
Novartis, Roche and Nestle led the market higher. ABB gained nine francs to 1,655.
Trade on Soffex centred on roll-over transactions in banks ahead of Friday's expiry. Implicit volatility was decreasing.
Index options were about 40 percent of total volume. In all 9,225 SMI futures were traded. The January SMI closed 38 points higher at 3,977 points.
